overview: Narrative review of the accuracy of symptom checker urgency advice, written for a lay committee, presenting vignette and real-user evidence separately and ending with requests for the two companies.
population: Studies from the last ten years that report urgency advice from publicly available symptom checker apps against a clinician or vignette reference.
exposure: Urgency advice from symptom checker apps, recorded by app and, where reported, by version.
procedures: The librarian searches three bibliographic databases and two sources of grey literature in October 2026. The investigator screens and extracts; the librarian checks a random 20 percent of screening decisions. Each study is classified as clinician-written vignette, lay-worded vignette or real-user, and results are tabulated by class. No company is contacted.

outcomes.name: Correct urgency level
outcomes.measure: Proportion of cases where app advice matched the reference urgency, reported by evidence class

outcomes.name: Under-triage of emergencies
outcomes.measure: Proportion of emergency cases advised a lower urgency

outcomes.name: Over-triage of self-care cases
outcomes.measure: Proportion of self-care cases advised to seek care

outcomes.name: Evidence class
outcomes.measure: Number of studies per class and with subgroup results for older adults, children and limited English
outcomes.why: Shows how thin the real-user evidence is.

feasibility: About 80 hours of the investigator's time and 12 librarian hours fit an expected 25 to 40 included studies.
biasMitigation: No pooling across classes or versions

biasFlags.label: Single reviewer
biasFlags.note: Partly mitigated by the librarian's check.

biasFlags.label: Version drift
biasFlags.note: Every figure is tied to an app version where reported.

parsimony.simplestPath: Three evidence classes, one table each, one page of requests for the companies.

theoreticalFramework: None; an evidence ladder from vignettes to real users organises the review.
summary: Narrative review protocol with evidence classes and a single reviewer checked by the librarian.
